pressure: Han defeat and recurring Xiongnu frontier pressure
material_flow: Fixed annual goods; later maxima under the agreement reached under 100000 liters of grain 200000 liters of wine and 92000 meters of silk
political_terms: Marriage alliance; coequal states; Great Wall as boundary
trade_access: Peace framework rather than a quantified market flow
limits: Terms changed over time and did not end every raid; the listed quantities are later maxima under the agreement not a first-year shipment.

polities: First Turkic Khaganate China and Byzantium
pressure: Chinese tribute left the Türk court with thousands of silk rolls and Sogdian merchants sought another outlet
material_flow: Thousands of silk rolls paid by China; no complete quantity series survives
political_terms: Türk-Sogdian diplomacy opened direct contact with Byzantium after a failed Sasanian approach
trade_access: A new western market for tribute silk
limits: One reported diplomatic-commercial episode does not measure total tribute total trade or the durability of the Byzantine connection.

pressure: Twenty-five years of war ended in a negotiated frontier order
material_flow: Each year 100000 ounces of silver and 200000 bolts of silk
political_terms: Mutual territorial claims set aside; diplomatic parity; no new border fortifications
trade_access: Border stability rather than a quantified trade volume
limits: Silver and silk retain their original unlike units and are not added as value; the agreement was durable but not permanent.

pressure: Western Xia battlefield success forced the Song to extend the Chanyuan model
material_flow: About 250000 annual units of silk silver and tea
political_terms: Yuanhao recognized as King of Western Xia with hereditary rights to lands already held
limits: The published total combines unlike units and is shown only as reported; the settlement did not resolve every frontier conflict.
